MC: Think Python, Chapter 14: Classes and Functions, question 2

These statements are intended to define a Date class and create a Date object. What is wrong with them?

def Date:
    """Represents a day of the year."""

date = Date()
date.year = 2024
date.month = 'January'
date.day = 11
column3: HTML
A class definition has to start with class, not def.
column5: A class definition has to start with class. A function definition starts with def.

column3: All of the attributes have to have the same type.
column5: The attributes of an object can be any type, and they don't have to be the same.

column3: You can't have a class named Date and a variable named date.
column5: It is legal -- and common -- for a class name and a variable to be the same word, but the class name starts with an uppercase letter.

column3: The syntax is not correct for adding attributes to the object.
column5: Dot notation is used to set the value of an attribute and to read the value.

MC: Think Python, Chapter 14: Classes and Functions, question 4

Suppose today refers to a Date object, and we run this code:

def set_date(date, val):
    date.date = val

set_date(today, 27)

Which of these is true afterward?
column3: HTML
The Date object that today refers to has an attribute called date whose value is 27.
column5: Inside the function, date refers to the same object as today, so date.date = val creates an attribute of that object. Functions like make_time in this chapter use the same names for parameters and attributes on purpose.

column3: The parameter date was changed to 27, but today is unchanged.
column5: date.date = val does not change the parameter date -- it still refers to the Date object -- and because date and today refer to the same object, the change is visible through today.

column3: today now refers to the integer 27.
column5: The function never assigns a new value to today or to date; it assigns to an attribute of the object they both refer to.

column3: It caused an error, because date is already the name of a parameter.
column5: A parameter and an attribute can have the same name without conflict: the parameter is a variable in the function's frame and the attribute belongs to the object.
